source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue the standard mattress and rely on repositioning alone because support-surface selection does not affect pressure-injury prevention.","B":"Reduce skin assessment frequency because repeated inspection increases friction and can worsen early sacral changes.","C":"Stop routine repositioning after adding a cushion because a pressure-relieving device replaces the need for position changes.","D":"Use an appropriate pressure-redistributing support surface while continuing individualized repositioning and regular skin assessment."}}
source_row.rationale: A high-risk client with early sacral skin changes needs a combined prevention approach. VA guidance supports regular skin inspection, repositioning, and appropriate support surfaces that reduce pressure. A support surface does not replace repositioning or surveillance, and a standard mattress should not be assumed adequate when skin changes are already emerging.
source_row.source_detail: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Take Steps to Prevent Pressure Injuries: inspect skin regularly, reposition according to risk/condition, and use appropriate pressure-reducing/support surfaces such as special mattresses, overlays, or cushions when indicated. Current VA Veterans Health Library pressure-injury prevention guidance; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: mobility, positioning, skin integrity, elimination and nonpharmacologic comfort activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A client at high risk for pressure injury is being repositioned regularly but has early sacral skin changes. Which additional intervention is most appropriate?
